sections.heading: What's Included
sections.intro: Everything a website needs to stay online, every day — with almost nothing for hackers to break into. No add-ons, no upsells.

items.label: Managed static hosting
items.body: Served from a network close to your customers — fast loading from anywhere

items.label: SSL certificate
items.body: HTTPS always on, auto-renewed, no expiry scares

items.label: Daily backups
items.body: We can restore the site quickly if anything goes sideways

items.label: 24/7 uptime monitoring

items.label: No plugin updates

sections.heading: Why Static Beats WordPress Here
sections.body: WordPress is powerful, but for a trade-business website, it's overkill, creates maintenance debt, and adds attack surface that doesn't earn its keep. Static sites eliminate that:
items: No plugins to update or conflict — and no third-party code touching your customer-facing surface
No admin panel to get compromised
No database to leak — there's literally nothing for an attacker to query
Loads in under a second, globally

sections.heading: Perfect For
sections.intro: If any of these are familiar, the boring infrastructure layer is exactly what's costing you sleep — and we take it off your plate entirely.

items.label: Hacked or held hostage by WordPress
items.body: Your site got compromised, defaced, or quietly turned into a spam farm — and your "web person" couldn't tell you what went wrong or guarantee it won't happen again.

items.label: Stacking $30+/mo plugin bills
items.body: Hosting is $15, the contact-form plugin is $9, the SEO plugin is $12, the security plugin is $20, and somehow you're paying $80/mo just to keep a brochure site online.

items.label: No time for updates, ever
items.body: You don't want a login. You don't want to remember to patch anything. You want to pay one bill and have it work for the next three years without thinking about it.

items.label: Site down when homeowners are looking
items.body: It went down on a Sunday evening when someone googled "emergency plumber near me," and you didn't notice until Monday. Uptime monitoring with someone who actually responds is non-negotiable.

items.label: Inherited a hosting mess
items.body: The previous owner / partner / friend-with-tech-skills set up hosting in their account, and nobody quite knows where the domain is registered or whose credit card is on file.

faqs.question: What uptime can you actually guarantee?
faqs.answer: Our hosting stack has tracked ~100% uptime across the sites we've launched. We don't sell a contractual SLA — small trade businesses don't need one — but our monitoring fires the second a site goes down and we respond fast.

faqs.question: How long are backups kept?
faqs.answer: Daily backups are retained for 30 days. Recovery from any backup point in that window takes minutes, not hours. We've never had to use one in production, but it's there.

faqs.question: What happens if my site does go down?
faqs.answer: We get the alert before you do. In most cases the issue is auto-resolved before it would even surface to a visitor. If we need to roll back to a backup, we do — and you get an email afterwards explaining what happened.

faqs.question: Can I move my existing domain?
faqs.answer: Yes. Your domain stays in your own registrar account — we never take ownership. We coordinate the DNS cutover at launch so there's no downtime, and your old site stays up until you're ready to switch.

faqs.question: Why don't I just use WordPress hosting?
faqs.answer: You can — but you're paying for a CMS layer your site doesn't need, and accepting attack surface a trade business doesn't want. WordPress hosting also means PHP version upgrades, plugin patches, and a login that needs protecting. Static sites have none of that surface area.
